h: Lower Basildon, the Thames and a Very Grand Neighbour
p: Beale sits at Lower Basildon, on the stretch of the Thames between Pangbourne and Goring, and it's a properly pretty bit of England. The river is wide and slow here, with wooded hills rising on either side of the valley, and that setting is a big part of what makes a visit feel like a holiday rather than a quick trip out.

Right across the road you'll find Basildon Park, a grand eighteenth-century National Trust house set in parkland. It's a smashing add-on for grown-ups who fancy some history, and the grounds are lovely for a walk. Fans of period dramas may recognise the house, as it has appeared on screen more than once.

Pangbourne, just down the road, has a nice little high street and a riverside meadow, and it's where Kenneth Grahame, author of The Wind in the Willows, spent his later years. Little ones who know Ratty, Mole and Toad might enjoy knowing they're in the right part of the world. Upstream, the twin villages of Goring and Streatley face each other across the river and are great for a pub lunch or a riverside stroll.

The Thames Path runs through this part of the valley too, so keen walkers can tie a visit into a longer ramble. Pangbourne has a railway station on the line from Reading, which makes it possible to reach the area without a car, though you'll need to plan the last stretch. It's a properly gentle, unhurried corner of Berkshire.
